_comment: Every piece of third-party code copied into this module, and where it came
from. This file is the single source of truth that NOTICE, each fork's
doc.go and the README state in prose: forks_test.go fails when the prose
and this file disagree, when a copied directory is missing an entry, and
when the recorded hash of an embedded file no longer matches it.
internal/forkcheck reads it to answer the only question that matters for
maintenance: has UPSTREAM moved since the fork point? It diffs upstream
against itself between fork_point and the newest release, never against
our copy -- a fork-versus-upstream diff is permanently noisy, because the
modifications are the point, so nobody reads it. Upstream against itself
is empty in the steady state, which makes a non-empty result a signal.
fork_point is history and does not move with Dependabot: the module's
x/crypto requirement rises for the rest of the package while a fork stays
where it was ported from. unchanged_through records the newest upstream
release checked to be identical in the copied paths, so the pair together
says 'ported from X, and upstream has not changed through Y'.
A goroot fork records the Go MINOR line, go1.26 and not go1.27.1, and the
check compares it as a prefix of the running toolchain's version. That is
deliberate: the identity test re-verifies against whichever toolchain runs,
and CI runs two exact patches on every pull request (the newest release
everywhere, the oldest supported on the ubuntu and windows test legs), so
the field documents reach rather than doing the verifying. Recording a
patch instead would report every Go patch release as something to update,
for a file that practically never changes, and a report that means nothing
is one nobody reads.
identity[] mirrors the claims in each fork's upstream_identity_test.go.
Those tests compare against the x/crypto the module RESOLVES; forkcheck
compares against the NEWEST release, so a changed upstream function is
seen before a dependency bump arrives, and even if none ever does.
Modes: bytes (exact), code (ignore comments, blank lines and the package
clause), func (one top-level function, comment lines dropped), block (a
regexp-delimited span, for golden tables).

forks.notes: Argon2 plus the portable BLAKE2b compression function and one-shot finalisation, modified so every byte of working state lives in a caller-owned Workspace and is wiped.
The KDF that protects OpenSSH private-key files, with Blowfish, modified to run in a caller-owned Workspace that can be a SecureBuffer.
The X25519 Montgomery ladder from the standard library's crypto/ecdh, callable on a scalar held in locked memory, with the field package pointed at filippo.io/edwards25519.
The EFF long wordlist, embedded byte-for-byte as distributed, under CC BY 3.0. Not code: the check is that the file still hashes to what NOTICE's claim of byte identity rests on.
